content: Use Kaggle T4 for any encoder-heavy task (builds, benchmarks, training). There is no local CUDA on this machine, so encoding more than a few thousand passages must go to a Kaggle GPU kernel.
The Anthropic API key is read from the CLAUDE_API environment variable, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Bench and judge code reads CLAUDE_API_2.
Never position rlat as 'RAG'. RAG is one downstream consumer; rlat is a queryable knowledge-model substrate — a semantic layer over unstructured data.
rlat is a context primer (about 18x faster at session start), not a search replacement; live tools are about 3.6x more complete on specific lookups. Position it as a primer, not a search engine.
Use the term 'knowledge model', never 'cartridge', in all new code, docs, and board items. The file extension stays .rlat.
Run the rigor skill (self-review, simplify, adversarial review, harness, empirical gate) before every commit. The old codex review is retired.

On Windows, every kaggle CLI invocation must be prefixed with PYTHONUTF8=1. Without it the CLI decodes responses as CP1252 and a charmap crash silently eats a successful push, leaving the slug unrecorded and status returning 403.
Always pass --accelerator NvidiaTeslaT4 when pushing a Kaggle kernel. Relying on enable_gpu alone may assign a P100 (sm_60), on which current PyTorch CUDA ops fail silently.
Re-run 'pip install -e .[dev]' after editing the source if the CLI shows stale behaviour. The installed entry point can lag working-tree edits.
Skills must live at .claude/skills/<name>/, never in a custom directory. The loader only discovers skills under that path.
Do not give timeline or duration estimates. Claude has no reliable sense of wall-clock time; human-training-data estimates mislead.
For a new benchmark, run a small deterministic search gate first and add the LLM judge later. Audit benchmarks/results and prior findings before designing any run.
RunPod and Kaggle orchestrators upload source via 'git archive HEAD', so uncommitted working-tree edits do not reach the pod. Commit fixes before launching a remote job.
The default encoder is Alibaba-NLP/gte-modernbert-base, 768-dim, CLS pooling + L2 normalisation, max sequence 8192, at a pinned Hugging Face revision.
Cross-knowledge-model operations (rlat compare, RQL compare/overlap/unique) always use the base band for compatibility, never the optimised band.

Value is usefulness, not recall. Retrieval/recall is not inherently valuable; meaning, the right information, better answers, and things that drive actions are. Do not measure recall@k or retrieval-AUC as if it were product value.

Local instruct/reasoning cores at or below 8B (Qwen2.5-instruct and DeepSeek-R1-distill alike) fail real multi-hop Fabric questions even when handed the gold passages — coverage 0.40-0.61 and grounding 0.58-0.77, all below the 0.90 floor that cloud Sonnet hits. The failure is grounding (they drift/hallucinate against in-context evidence), not retrieval. The reasoner-dependent local-answer line (H1/H1a) is KILLed for both model classes; route to per-link grounding on a cloud path instead.

Any decoder-only / causal embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding family, E5-mistral, GritLM, NV-Embed) must use last-non-padding-token pooling, never mean or CLS. Mean pooling collapsed Qwen3-8B BEIR-5 from 0.500 to 0.250 (7x on fiqa). The signature of a wrong-pooling preset is: long-query corpora roughly OK, short-query corpora (fiqa/nfcorpus/scidocs) collapse 3-7x. Encoder-only BERT-family models (BGE, E5-large, GTE) keep mean/CLS.

Do not default to enabling a cross-encoder reranker on top of a strong dense retriever. bge-reranker-v2-m3 and mxbai-rerank-base-v1 regress Qwen3-8B on 4 of 5 BEIR corpora (and regressed every MRL config on a Fabric held-out set) because they were trained on weaker base retrievers' candidate sets and see a mismatched input distribution. The real driver is query-distribution alignment with the reranker's training data, not encoder strength; default-always-rerank is wrong. Probe per-corpus.

Never fine-tune the encoder on MS MARCO and ship it as the default. The ft-bge-large-v1-stage1 MS MARCO fine-tune regressed 4 of 5 BEIR corpora (avg -8.3pt, worst on arguana -14.4pt and fiqa -13.6pt) and failed Gate 1 (0.4524 < 0.47). MS MARCO is web-search short-query distribution and overfits away from academic/argumentative corpora. Match training distribution to the target retrieval workload; the preset stays opt-in only.

Tiered/recency-weighted memory and adaptive prefer-recent post-processing are mutually exclusive — running both double-counts recency and causes knowledge-update cliffs. Tiered LayeredMemory regressed LoCoMo -11pt aggregate (multi-hop and temporal both -27pt) and LME showed the same -0.100 KU cliff. The cartridge-per-conversation baseline (68.2% on LoCoMo) beats the tiered approach regardless of retrieval features.

Do not re-fire the LongMemEval 'full-stack' retrieval features on LoCoMo, especially subgraph/spectral-neighbour expansion. On a ~150-chunk per-conversation cartridge, subgraph expansion craters single-hop -30pt (neighbours become effectively everything). Feeding LLM-extracted facts in as separate context rows also fails — they displace raw chunks in top-k (single-hop -43pt); facts must be a ranking-time bias on raw chunks, not separate documents.

Retrieval-time EML scoring/fusion knobs (enable_eml_sharpen, eml_alpha, eml_fusion, etc.) are falsified three separate times — exp(alpha*x) numerically dominates the -ln term so the operator collapses to exp_only, or overflows to NaN. Do not retry EML as a retrieval scoring mechanism. The user-facing query-time spectral transforms --sharpen/--soften/--contrast/--tune are a SEPARATE feature and must not be removed alongside the retrieval cluster.

The memory importance model is a multi-factor salience function importance = f(recency, recurrence, criticality, trust), not a single sort key — any one factor can dominate (a critical hot-stove memory persists even when old and non-recurring; trust gates the rest). The working/episodic/semantic layering was ABANDONED; the live structure is the kind ladder event -> pattern -> learning -> principle. Do not collapse ranking to cosine-plus-recency and do not resurrect the tier hierarchy.

The earned-knowledge thesis is TWO loops, not one: Loop 1 (per-session Notice/Judge/Update/Recall) is reputation — it ranks what already exists; Loop 2 (periodic Distil: events->patterns->learnings->principles) is synthesis — it derives new beliefs. Loop 2 is the real earned-knowledge layer. Adding synthesis on top of an unfinished Loop 1 substrate, then measuring it with a retrieval-grain benchmark, was the documented Phase B/4 mistake — do not repeat it.

Capture and insight must live INSIDE the .rlat archive (a ZIP member, buffered then flushed), never in a sidecar file or a separate .rlat-state/ ledger — a sidecar violates the self-contained moat. Capture is always-on (not opt-in, no setup gate); only the LLM is opt-in (required just to grow the corpus, with graceful degradation to retrieve-plus-remember without it). The insight band is on-by-default with explicit-disable, never default-off-needs-enable.

The insight-engine product moat is verifiable AND cheap insight (trust + cost), NOT better-than-LLM quality — five experiments established that explicit structure does not out-reason a capable LLM on insight quality (small-context conflict surfacing even LOST 90%/26% to a conflict-prompted LLM). Trust = claims extracted from source spans, content-hashed, drift-tracked, reproducible (free LLM-RAG measured ~0% reproducible across runs). Cost = precompute once at build with cheap local models, amortized across queries. The win is for frequently-queried corpora; one-shot queries still favor the LLM.

Detecting answer gaps from retrieval fingerprints (top-k cosine scores) is falsified on a densely-covered corpus and independently confirmed: removing the answer doc barely moves the score because topically-adjacent sibling docs still match high (gap vs non-gap top-1 0.774 vs 0.813, 0/54 gaps fell below the 0.30 retrieval-failed floor). No LLM-free signal (geometry, encoder, distilled tiny cross-encoder) clears ~0.73 AUC; the gap lives in answer-quality/text semantics, not geometry. Gap detection requires a READ — a ~7B local instruct reader doing gold-free answerability matches the cloud Haiku teacher (~0.79-0.81) and is corpus-agnostic; encoders cap at the retrieval floor.

The semantic-lattice graph-walk is NOT a retrieval win. The apparent Fabric why/which lift (hit@10 67%->100%) was a length artifact: the walk SUMs structural boost over a doc's claims so long docs win, and it tested significantly HARMFUL on BEIR (-0.05 to -0.38 nDCG@10 with SUM; MAX is corpus-dependent with no transfer). Flat claim retrieval also regresses vs passages — claims are a structure layer OVER passages, not a retrieval unit. The live track is answer assembly from the subgraph, not re-ranking.

Resonance Lattice ships under Business Source License (BSL) — source-available, commercial use allowed from day one EXCEPT building a competing product during the exclusivity window — with a planned commercial SaaS layer on top. BSL is NOT non-commercial. Any artifact that may be redistributed commercially must use an Apache-2.0/MIT/BSD/CC-BY-compatible license; CC BY-NC sources (NV-Embed-v2, FiQA, some BEIR corpora) taint derivatives and are research-only. Use a dual-track research-vs-production split when a better-but-NC option exists.

Before any REMOVE verdict on a module flagged 'unreachable' by a static AST audit, runtime-verify it: grep for lazy/in-function imports, check the __init__.py _LAZY_IMPORTS/_LAZY_SYMBOLS string table (invisible to AST walkers), import-then-getattr the symbol, and grep docs/ for documented public APIs (a product surface even with no src/ importer). The static audit was only ~30% reliable — six confirmed misses (wizard_ui, subspace, skill_projector, reranker_openvino, temporal, temporal_algebra). Note also that src/resonance_lattice/memory.py (ResonanceMemory) is legacy/unwired; the production memory path is layered_memory.py (LayeredMemory).

Any cache keyed on corpus-specific indices — MRL synthetic queries (passage_idx), passage embeddings, hard-negative pairs — must be scoped under benchmarks/results/<corpus_name>/ and looked up by corpus name, never reused 'most recent across all runs'. Cross-corpus reuse silently makes every training positive a random passage; loss sticks at ln(num_passages) and dev R@1 collapses to zero. If a cache file carries no corpus identifier, regenerate rather than reuse it.
